content: Coffee beans are the seeds of the coffee fruit, often called a cherry. There are two main commercially grown coffee species: Arabica and Robusta. Arabica beans are known for their sweet, complex flavor profiles with notes of fruit, chocolate, and nuts. They grow at higher elevations (600-2000 meters) and contain less caffeine than Robusta. Robusta beans have a stronger, more bitter taste with earthy and woody notes. They contain about twice as much caffeine as Arabica and are more resistant to pests and diseases. The flavor of coffee beans is influenced by factors such as growing region, altitude, soil conditions, processing method, and roast level.
